Path Traversal in SPA Catch-All File Server — Arbitrary file read from any path accessible to the server process, including /etc/passwd, application secrets, and SSH keys. [verified: Identical root cause as finding [0]: `frontend_dist / path` in the SPA catch-all at app/main.py:47-49 allows URL-encoded `..` traversal (e.g., `/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/etc/passwd`) that Starlette passes decoded to the handler, constructing a path outside `frontend_dist` that passes both `.exists()` and `.is_file()` checks before being served via `FileResponse` with no boundary validation. Confirmed exploit]

IDOR: API key holder can update any organization's ticket status — Cross-tenant data manipulation; an integration for one org can alter or close tickets belonging to other orgs. [verified: The PATCH /api/integrations/tickets/{ticket_id}/status endpoint fetches tickets purely by integer primary key (db.get(Ticket, ticket_id)) with no ownership check, and the ApiKey model has no organization_id field, so any active API key can modify tickets belonging to any other organization. No middleware, decorator, or inline check enforces tenant scoping on this endpoint.]

IDOR — Cross-Tenant Ticket Status Update via Integration API — An integration API key holder from one organization can transition tickets (e.g., close, reopen, resolve) belonging to any other organization, disrupting SLA tracking and support operations across tenants. [verified: Confirmed: api_key_auth only validates that the key is active and updates last_used_at; it does not bind the key to an organization. The status-update handler never compares ticket.organization_id against the key creator's organization, unlike the sibling create_ticket_from_api endpoint, leaving full cross-tenant ticket manipulation open to any valid API key holder.]

Client-Supplied Content-Type Enables Stored XSS via Attachment Download — Persistent XSS in application origin via malicious attachment; full session theft and arbitrary actions as victim user. [verified: The persist_upload function (services.py:222) stores the client-supplied upload.content_type verbatim, and the download_attachment endpoint (tickets.py:253) serves it back with media_type=attachment.content_type via FileResponse. Although FileResponse sets Content-Disposition: attachment via the filename parameter, there is no X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff header anywhere in the application, no ]

Path Traversal and Unencrypted PAN/SSN Storage in /ops/vault endpoint — Arbitrary file write anywhere writable by the server process; exposure of unencrypted credit card numbers and SSNs violating PCI DSS. [verified: ticket_vault_stash_243 uses unvalidated ref param for path construction and writes plaintext SSN/card — both path traversal and unencrypted PII/PAN storage confirmed, duplicate of findings 4 and 16.]

Plaintext PII/PAN (SSN, card number) written to disk — Attacker or insider who reads the export directory obtains raw SSNs and card numbers; PCI DSS / GDPR violation [verified: ticket_vault_stash_243 writes SSN and card numbers as plaintext JSON to disk — confirmed unencrypted PII/PAN storage, duplicate of finding 16.]

SSN and credit card numbers stored in plaintext on disk — PII/PAN exposure if the filesystem is accessed by an attacker, insider, or backup systems; regulatory violation. [verified: ticket_vault_stash_243 writes SSN and raw card numbers as plaintext JSON to disk with no encryption, confirmed in source at the write_text call. This violates PCI-DSS and privacy regulations regardless of path traversal.]

CORS: arbitrary Origin reflected with Allow-Credentials true — Cross-origin attacker site can make credentialed requests and read responses, enabling CSRF-equivalent data exfiltration [verified: ticket_origin_mirror_562 reflects Origin verbatim as Access-Control-Allow-Origin with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true — confirmed CORS misconfiguration enabling cross-origin credentialed requests, duplicate of finding 7.]

Server-Side Template Injection via fragment parameter — Arbitrary Python code execution as the application user; full server compromise. [verified: ticket_jinja_cast_582 concatenates user-supplied `fragment` directly into a Jinja2 Template source string before rendering, enabling full SSTI/RCE. The only protection is the _wrk_gate static token check.]

Path Traversal enabling arbitrary file write via name parameter — Overwrite application source files or OS files writable by the process user, enabling persistent backdoor or denial of service. [verified: ticket_dock_shelf_591 constructs `target = BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name` using pathlib, which does NOT strip `..` segments (only absolute paths override the base). A name like `../../app/main.py` resolves outside BASE_EXPORT_DIR and write_bytes overwrites arbitrary files accessible to the process.]

NoSQL injection via unvalidated MongoDB query filter from request body — Unauthorized data access, query manipulation, or denial of service against the MongoDB instance. [verified: ticket_mongo_lane_612 passes payload.get('filter', payload) directly as a MongoDB find_one query with no sanitization, allowing injection of MongoDB operators ($where, $gt, etc.) for data exfiltration or DoS. Gated only by static shared INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN.]

OS Command Injection via host query parameter — Remote code execution on the server; full system compromise by any caller who knows INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN. [verified: ticket_shell_probe_632 passes unsanitized `host` query parameter directly to `_os.system('ping -c 1 ' + host)`. The only gate is _wrk_gate (X-Internal-Token check), which is a shared static secret — any holder can inject shell metacharacters for OS command execution.]

NoSQL Injection via MongoDB query operator injection — Bypass query filters to read arbitrary documents from the MongoDB collection; potential DoS or data exfiltration [verified: ticket_mongo_lane_612 passes user-controlled dict directly as MongoDB filter with no sanitization — confirmed NoSQL injection, duplicate of finding 12.]

OS Command Injection via host parameter — Full remote code execution on the server; attacker can read/write files, exfiltrate data, pivot to internal network [verified: ticket_shell_probe_632 (same endpoint as idx 0) passes unsanitized `host` to _os.system('ping -c 1 ' + host) — confirmed OS command injection, duplicate of finding 0 but independently true.]

OS Command Injection via /ops/shell endpoint — Full remote code execution with the web server's OS privileges; persistent backdoor, lateral movement. [verified: ticket_shell_probe_632 passes unsanitized `host` to _os.system() — confirmed OS command injection, duplicate of finding 0.]

Session cookie Secure flag disabled by default — Session tokens transmitted in cleartext over HTTP; vulnerable to passive interception on any non-TLS network. [verified: app/config.py line 26 defaults `secure_cookies` to False, and .env.example explicitly ships `SECURE_COOKIES=false`; app/routers/auth.py passes `secure=settings.secure_cookies` to `response.set_cookie`, so session cookies are issued without the Secure flag by default, exposing them to interception over HTTP.]

No rate limiting or brute-force protection on authentication endpoints — Credential brute-force; account takeover via offline or online password guessing attacks. [verified: No rate limiting middleware (no slowapi, fastapi-limiter, or equivalent) is present in requirements.txt or registered in main.py; only CORSMiddleware is added. Login and password-reset endpoints accept unlimited unauthenticated requests with no throttle, lockout, or CAPTCHA.]

Hardcoded demo credentials and API key in seed script — Anyone with the source code can authenticate as the demo admin or use the seeded API key against any seeded environment [verified: DEMO_PASSWORD and DEMO_API_KEY are unconditionally hardcoded string literals in app/seed.py with no environment-variable override, and both are printed in plaintext to stdout after seeding; the API key is stored hashed but the plaintext is publicly known from source. Any environment that ran the seed script has a publicly-known admin password and integration API key, making authentication trivial ]

CSV Formula Injection in Ticket Export — A malicious user who crafts a ticket subject starting with '=' can inject spreadsheet formulas into exported CSV files, potentially exfiltrating data from support staff's spreadsheet applications or executing arbitrary code when the file is opened. [verified: The csv_response function at services.py:291 uses csv.DictWriter with default QUOTE_MINIMAL quoting and writes user-controlled fields (ticket.subject, requester.email) directly into CSV without stripping formula-injection prefixes (=, +, -, @). No sanitization exists anywhere in the codebase, so a ticket subject like '=HYPERLINK("http://evil.com","click")' would appear verbatim in the exported fil]

Reflected XSS via Raw HTML Concatenation in /ops/copy endpoint — Execution of arbitrary JavaScript in victim's browser; session theft, phishing. [verified: ticket_bannerlet_088 concatenates copyline directly into HTML string returned as HTMLResponse — confirmed reflected XSS, duplicate of finding 5.]

Reflected XSS via unescaped copyline parameter in HTML response — Session hijacking, credential theft, or browser-based exploitation of any user tricked into visiting the crafted URL. [verified: ticket_bannerlet_088 directly concatenates `copyline` into an HTML string returned as HTMLResponse with no escaping, enabling reflected XSS. The _wrk_gate requires INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN, limiting the attacker surface to token holders who trick an authenticated victim into clicking the URL.]

Mass assignment allowing role/admin flag escalation — Attacker-controlled role/admin/credit values returned in response; if this workset is persisted or trusted downstream, privilege escalation occurs [verified: ticket_panel_rebind_089 merges the full JSON request body into a workset dict containing role, is_admin, and credit_limit via workset.update(change_set), allowing an attacker to overwrite these security-sensitive fields. The response returns the merged workset; if trusted downstream this enables privilege escalation.]

Open Redirect via /ops/after endpoint — Phishing attacks using trusted domain as redirect hop; potential SSRF probing of internal network resources. [verified: ticket_return_lane_160 passes lane param directly to RedirectResponse — confirmed open redirect, duplicate of finding 6. SSRF to internal metadata endpoints is also plausible.]

Bearer token and request body logged at WARNING level — Exposure of session tokens or API keys in log stores; allows session hijacking or API key replay attacks [verified: ticket_wire_tally_221 logs full request body and Authorization header (bearer token) at WARNING level — confirmed sensitive data in logs, duplicate of finding 10. Log injection via newlines in body is also a valid concern.]

Reflected XSS via card parameter with |safe filter — Arbitrary JavaScript execution in victim's browser; session hijacking, credential theft, CSRF [verified: ticket_blurb_tile_325 uses Template('{{ card|safe }}').render(card=card) and returns HTMLResponse — the |safe filter marks card as HTML-safe and injects it verbatim, so any HTML/JS in card is reflected unescaped. This is confirmed reflected XSS (not SSTI as the card value is a template variable, not concatenated into template source).]

Privilege escalation via unverified ops_badge cookie/header — Any user can claim elevated role by setting a cookie or header, gaining access to payroll and casework data. [verified: ticket_badge_gate_622 grants elevated payroll/casework access based solely on attacker-controlled cookie ops_badge or header x-ops-badge with value 'lead' — no signature, HMAC, or server-side session validation is performed. Any INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN holder can self-elevate by setting the header.]

Insecure PRNG (random module) used for token/nonce generation — Predictable tokens enable session/nonce forgery if the PRNG state can be inferred from observed outputs. [verified: ticket_nonce_roll_602 uses Python's random.choice() (Mersenne Twister, non-CSPRNG) to generate nonce/code values. If these codes are used for security purposes (tokens, CSRF, reset codes), the PRNG state is recoverable after ~624 observations enabling prediction.]

Weak PRNG (random.choice) used for nonce/token generation — Attacker can predict generated nonces/codes if PRNG state is recoverable; undermines any security use of these values [verified: ticket_nonce_roll_602 uses random.choice() (Mersenne Twister) for nonce generation — confirmed weak PRNG, duplicate of finding 13.]

Client-Controlled Authorization Header/Cookie Grants Elevated Access — Unauthorized access to sensitive payroll and casework information by any caller of the ops endpoint. [verified: ticket_badge_gate_622 grants elevated access based on attacker-controlled cookie/header — confirmed missing authorization, duplicate of finding 9.]

Broken Access Control via Attacker-Controlled Badge Header — An INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN holder can self-escalate to the 'lead' privilege tier by forging a header value, gaining access to payroll and casework data without holding a legitimately issued credential. [verified: ticket_badge_gate_622 grants elevated access based solely on attacker-controlled cookie or header with no signature/HMAC validation — confirmed broken access control, duplicate of finding 9.]

Account Enumeration via Login Timing Difference and Registration Error Messages — Attacker can enumerate valid account emails to target for credential stuffing or spear phishing. [verified: When a user is not found, the login short-circuit skips the PBKDF2 hash check entirely (no dummy verify call), creating a measurable timing difference vs a valid user with a wrong password; additionally, registration returns a distinct HTTP 409 `'Email is already registered'` that directly confirms account existence.]

User Enumeration via Registration Endpoint — Attacker can enumerate valid user email addresses, enabling targeted credential-stuffing, phishing, or password-reset abuse against confirmed accounts. [verified: The register endpoint explicitly returns HTTP 409 with distinct messages: `'Email is already registered'` vs `'Organization already exists; ask an admin for an invite'`, unambiguously confirming account existence to any unauthenticated caller iterating email addresses.]

Weak MD5 Hash Used for Cryptographic Digest — Hash collisions trivially constructable; stored hashes reversible via rainbow tables; any integrity or authentication use is bypassed. [verified: ticket_digest_fold_281 uses hashlib.md5() — confirmed weak/broken cryptographic hash, duplicate of finding 14.]

Security headers explicitly disabled (XSS protection, CSP cleared) — Browser XSS filters and CSP enforcement disabled for affected responses; increases exploitability of any XSS finding [verified: ticket_frame_slip_572 explicitly sets X-XSS-Protection: 0 and Content-Security-Policy: '' — confirmed intentional removal of browser XSS defenses, duplicate of finding 8.]

Internal environment variables and filesystem path exposed in API response — Reconnaissance aid for attackers; reveals deployment environment and directory structure to target further attacks. [verified: ticket_trace_panel_642 returns os.environ.get('APP_ENV') and str(BASE_EXPORT_DIR) in its JSON response, leaking deployment environment name and absolute filesystem path — useful reconnaissance for path traversal payload construction.]

Internal environment variable and filesystem path disclosed in response — Attacker learns deployment environment and absolute export path, enabling more precise path traversal and targeted attacks [verified: ticket_trace_panel_642 returns str(BASE_EXPORT_DIR) and APP_ENV env var — confirmed information disclosure aiding path traversal, duplicate of finding 15.]

Internal Filesystem Path and Environment Info Disclosed via /ops/trace — Assists path traversal attacks by revealing server filesystem layout; confirms debug/trace mode is permanently enabled. [verified: ticket_trace_panel_642 returns BASE_EXPORT_DIR absolute path and APP_ENV env var — confirmed information disclosure aiding path traversal attacks, duplicate of finding 15.]
